result.title: Was the Model Given the Right Action? Auditing and Repairing Action Interfaces in Navigation World Models
result.summary: World models are evaluated by predicting future observations from actions. These evaluations assume that actions are prepared the same way as during training, but an unchecked mismatch can make a model appear less accurate than it is. We audit this assumption in Navigation World Models (NWM) and find three interacting differences between its training and rollout code. Correcting the inputs, without retraining, reduces mean visual prediction error by 42%, measured with DreamSim on the RECON navigation dataset. The correction also changes the ranking of NWM checkpoints in an exploratory analysis and removes or reduces two alternative models' measured advantages. Correcting only the normalization offset instead increases error, showing why interacting mismatches must be checked together. To test whether sensitivity to input preparation extends beyond NWM, we deliberately introduce encoding errors into two alternative models; both become less accurate. We introduce ActRosetta, a tool that checks whether action encoding matches training, identifies supported causes of disagreement, and repairs inputs when sufficient information is available. Repair helps little where predictions barely respond to actions, the tool's diagnosis has limited coverage, and improved control remains unproven. For any action-conditioned world model, the lesson is the same: before reporting rollout error, verify that evaluation encodes actions exactly as training did.

AI.brief_summary: 论文审计 Navigation World Models 中动作在训练与 rollout 阶段编码方式不一致的问题，指出这会低估模型表现，并提出 ActRosetta 工具诊断原因、修复输入，未重训即把视觉预测误差降低 42%。
AI.relevance_reason: 「先核查输入准备是否与训练一致、再报告 rollout 误差与检查点排序」的评测审计思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据或 latent 输入在训练与推理路径不一致时对误差指标、模型比较和贡献归属的干扰。
